profile.reading:
Open Data Centers operates a carrier neutral colocation facility at 15 Corporate Place South in Piscataway, New Jersey, a suburban office park in Middlesex County roughly sixteen miles south of New York City. The operator markets the site to network carriers, service providers and enterprise customers looking for connectivity focused colocation space outside Manhattan and northern New Jersey's more expensive core markets.

According to the operator's own site, the facility offers true A and B power distribution with up to 120 watts per square foot available to customer cabinets, along with a choice of AC or DC power feeds, a detail that points to a customer base that includes telecommunications equipment traditionally run on DC power alongside standard enterprise AC gear. Open Data Centers describes N+1 redundancy across its infrastructure and, in newer or expanded space within the building, 2N electrical and mechanical design, indicating that reliability specifications vary by suite rather than applying uniformly across the entire facility.

Connectivity is a central part of the pitch. The site lists access to multiple dark fiber providers, including Sunesys, Zayo and Lightower, along with lit service from carriers such as Verizon, Level 3 and Cogent, plus additional internet service providers and nearby fiber routes from FiberTech and Cross River Fiber. The operator maintains a staffed network operations center around the clock and describes full physical security systems protecting the space.

The building saw at least one documented tenant expansion in 2016, when the WebSite Source unit of 1stPoint Communications grew its footprint inside the facility, a data point suggesting the site has hosted hosting and managed services providers in addition to pure network carriers. Beyond that expansion, the operator's site does not publish a founding date, total building square footage, generator capacity, or a customer list, and no permit filings, news coverage or trade press specific to this Corporate Place South address were found describing the building's construction history or the ownership of the underlying property.

Piscataway sits within New Jersey's Route 1 and Route 287 technology corridor, an area with a long history of corporate research and telecommunications facilities. Open Data Centers' positioning, smaller and more carrier focused than the large wholesale campuses elsewhere in the state, reflects that corridor's role as a secondary but well connected alternative to the major northern New Jersey data center hubs.

reading.body:
This facility's published power specifications are not available in the data provided. The address places it in Piscataway, New Jersey, within Middlesex County, but the operator details and power capacity cannot be confirmed from the source listed.

New Jersey has 48 mapped data center facilities across the state, of which only five publish power capacity figures totaling 111.3 MW. This campus ranks sixth by published megawatts in the state, which means it either publishes a capacity below the fifth-ranked facility or is included in the ranking despite having no published specification in the current dataset, indicating a data inconsistency that requires resolution.

Without published power specifications, IT load, or certification details, this facility cannot be assessed for its relevance to AI infrastructure scaling. The research status is marked exhausted, meaning standard lookups have not returned operator-level details or technical specifications beyond the address.
